narrative.intro: United Concordia has $371M in federal contract obligations for FY2026 to date across 8 awards with an average award size of $46.4M. Obligations are down 7.9% year over year. Fiscal-year obligations moved from $438M in FY21 to $507M in FY22, then to $384M in FY23, $387M in FY24, $403M in FY25 and $371M in FY26 to date. The Department of Defense is the largest buyer, obligating $372M in the current-year records. Current-year totals are partial because FY2026 is not complete, and the published award totals reflect obligations rather than total contract values except where tables are labeled otherwise. These figures show United Concordia’s recent obligation levels, award count, and average award size, which you can use to benchmark the vendor against peers and to identify where federal buying is concentrated in the current fiscal period.

sections.heading: How have United Concordia obligations changed across recent fiscal years?
sections.body: Obligations rose from $438M in FY21 to $507M in FY22, then fell to $384M in FY23 before inching to $387M in FY24 and $403M in FY25. Obligations in FY26 are $371M to date, down 7.9% year over year compared with the prior fiscal-year period.

sections.heading: Which federal agencies are the largest buyers of United Concordia?
sections.body: The Department of Defense is the largest buying agency, with $372M in obligations in FY2026 to date. The available top-buyers listing identifies agencies by obligation totals; use that list to prioritize outreach to high-spend buyers.
